transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herbst.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky says he found it strange
that President Trump calls Russian leader Vladimir Putin a friend.
NPR's Joanna Kekissis reports Zelensky also addressed the recent
Ukrainian attack on a Russian warship.
Speaking to the BBC's Sarah Rainsford, Zelensky criticized
Trump's friendly greeting of Putin at the recent trilateral summit in China.
Zelensky compared Putin to Adolf Hitler.
He's an aggressor and a killer. He can't be a friend.
It's the same that somebody say about Hitler during the Second World War
that he's a good friend. No.
Meanwhile, Zelensky also said Ukraine had coordinated with nearby countries
when Ukrainian sea drones attacked a Russian warship off the coast of Libya.
Italy's foreign minister, though, told local media that Italy,
which is near Libya, was not informed.
Joanna Kekissis, NPR News, KU.
Today is the busiest shopping day of the year,
but many people wonder about the quality of the deals and the discounts.
And here's Alina Seljuk reports forecasts suggest they'll be similar to last year.
Several groups this year released research suggesting that many sales
only masquerade as discounts, and shopping experts always recommend
knowing in advance what the typical price is for something you plan to buy on Black Friday.
Adobe Analytics tracks actual spending and prices, specifically online,
and the group predicts that Black Friday is likely to have the biggest discounts
for toys, clothes, appliances, furniture, and televisions.
Meanwhile, Cyber Monday might have better discounts for computers and other electronics.
Top discounts are expected to be from 18 to 30 percent.
Alina Seljuk, NPR News.
This year's Atlantic hurricane season ends on Monday.
NPR's Debbie Elliott says 2026 has been one of the quietest years on record
for tropical activity.
The 2026 Atlantic hurricane season saw ten named storms,
but only one of them reached hurricane strength.
That was the late-forming Isaias that struck the Florida panhandle
as a powerful Category 2 hurricane in early October
and also caused damage in Alabama.
Cleanup is still underway along parts of the Gulf Coast.
Forecasters at Colorado State University say only one hurricane
is the fewest in more than a century, driven primarily by a strong El Nino weather pattern.
That's when extremely warm Pacific Ocean temperatures dampen Atlantic hurricane activity.
Debbie Elliott, NPR News, Orange Beach, Alabama.
While straight higher by the closing bell on this holiday-shortened trading week,
the Dow up 591, NASDAQ up 543.
For the NASDAQ, that's up 2.3 percent.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
The Iraqi government is closing border crossings run by Kurdish government forces,
and here's Jane Arav reports it's a controversial move
to take back control from the Kurdistan region.
Iraqi state media says border forces have closed a crossing with Syria
and another with Iran and territory administered by the Kurdish regional government.
Kurds broke away from central government control under Saddam Hussein in 1992
and now administer four majority Kurdish-Iraqi provinces, including border operations.
Earlier this week, the Iraqi prime minister announced that the federal oil ministry
would now run some of the biggest oil fields that are currently managed
by Iraq's Kurdistan regional government.
The government accuses Kurds of diverting oil proceeds.
They deny it.
The Kurdish leadership says it will not give up control of its borders or the oil fields.
Jane Arav, NPR News, Amman.
And Kurdish leaders have rejected Baghdad's moves as unilateral,
sparking protests in Erbil.
The U.N. has urged both sides to use caution.
The U.S. military says it disabled another ship in the Gulf of Oman
that tried to breach the U.S. naval blockade on Iranian ports.
U.S. Central Command says the MV Pacific Archer was disabled yesterday
and that the civilian crew was unharmed.
The MV Pacific Archer is at least the 15th disclosed vessel
to be disabled by the U.S. military since the blockade began in the spring.
I'm Janine Herbst, NPR News, in Washington.

topics.text: Zelensky calls Putin an aggressor and killer, compares him to Hitler in BBC interview
Ukraine sea drone attack on Russian warship off Libya; Italy says it was not informed
Black Friday shopping deals expected to match last year, with 18-30 percent discounts
Atlantic hurricane season ends with only one hurricane, Isaias, the fewest in a century
Dow and NASDAQ close higher on holiday-shortened trading week
Iraq closes border crossings run by Kurdish government forces, sparking controversy
Iraq moves to take over oil fields managed by Kurdistan regional government
U.S. military disables MV Pacific Archer in Gulf of Oman breaching Iranian port blockade
